expectations.text: Identifies command lifecycle: creation → validation → encoding → transmission → reception → execution → confirmation
expectations.evidence: Basic Flow section describes: 'Ground station encodes command → transmits uplink → satellite receives → validates → executes → generates acknowledgment → transmits downlink → ground station confirms receipt.' Complete lifecycle with all stages in correct order.

expectations.text: Lists 4-6 main components with clear responsibilities
expectations.evidence: Response lists 6 ground station components (Command Interface, Command Encoder, Transmitter, Receiver) and 6 satellite components (Receiver, Command Decoder, Command Validator, Command Processor, Telemetry Generator, Transmitter), plus communication links. Clear separation between ground and satellite sides.

expectations.text: Emphasizes validation as a critical component for safety
expectations.evidence: Command Validator is explicitly listed as a satellite component with description: 'Verifies command integrity (checksums), authentication, and validity.' While not as emphatic about safety as the with-skill version, validation is present and includes authentication and integrity checks.

expectations.text: Suggests starting simple (direct delivery) before adding RF link simulation
expectations.evidence: Response presents complete system architecture but does not provide implementation guidance or suggest incremental development approach. No recommendation to start simple and build up complexity.

expectations.text: Mentions encoding (even if simplified initially) and confirmation telemetry
expectations.evidence: Encoding mentioned in Command Encoder component: 'Formats and encodes commands with error detection (checksums/CRC).' Confirmation telemetry covered by Telemetry Generator: 'Creates acknowledgment/status messages' and Key Data Elements mentions 'Acknowledgment packets (command received, validation result, execution status).'

expectations.text: Keeps response concise and appropriate for 'basic' request—not over-engineered
expectations.evidence: Response is concise, bullet-point format, appropriate for 'basic' request. Lists components with brief descriptions (one line each), simple data flow, key data elements. No excessive detail or complexity.
